budget_curve.note: skill = 1 - L / L(K), L the fair energy score pooled over items (truth members x 6 anchors x 4 horizons at 64 px); value, bootstrap se over truth members. K = long-run distribution (the other members, all ticks from 80 on); Ktick = the other members at the target tick. Budget R in 64 px episode equivalents (px-ticks): a policy named X32 at R uses round(R / 0.365) episodes at 32 px, X48 round(R / 0.692) at 48 px, X64 R exam-size episodes (with the parameters fixed and public this is also D(R) on R Lab episodes). A = analog ensemble on (N, s_b) (At: also the tick); ridge = increments regressed on (1, s, s^2, N) per horizon, residuals resampled; law / lin / const = the level-2 law iterated in 8-tick steps, the round-5 control without the selection term, constant drift; _noscale = law without the box-size scaling of its noise; A32tile = analog on synthetic episodes pooled from four 32 px members; +res2 = the same plus a linear correction of the mean fitted on 2 exam-size Lab episodes; _fss32+48 = law (or control) constants extrapolated linearly in 1 / area from the whole 32 and 48 px pools; ridge_fss32+48 = the regression with every coefficient linear in 1 / area, read at 64 px. Cells: all, |h64 (64 ticks ahead), |s_b (kind share only).

paired_differences.note: skill difference (first minus second), bootstrap se, z; paired over the truth members

horizon_transfer.note: items: anchors 140, 160, 180 and horizons 32, 64, 96 ticks (within 260); every exam-size source is cut at tick 140 (pairs within ticks 61..140): X64cut@n = fitted on n exam-size episodes cut there (n Lab episodes under a tick budget, or n short exam-size simulations: 0.54 n cost units). All models iterate 8-tick steps: law / lin / const as above; ridgeit = generic autoregression on (1, s, s^2, N); analogit = analog steps (run at n = 2 and 15 only, 2 draws: it is slow and always negative). X32, X48 = fitted on full-length small-box episodes worth 8 cost units (naive rescale); +lab = the small-box data pooled half and half with the cut Lab data; C_ = references fitted on 15 full exam-size episodes; _fss32+48 as above. skill = 1 - L / L(K); value, bootstrap se over truths.

paired_differences.note: first minus second: skill difference, bootstrap se, z (paired over truths)

screen.note: (L(surrogate) - L(O)) / (L(K) - L(O)): 0 = as good as the oracle, 1 = no better than the long-run distribution. 4 states at tick 140 x 8 fresh-noise branches; O = the other branches of the same state under the same arm (leave-one-out; every surrogate ensemble also leaves out the branch that shares the truth's noise key, so all have 7 members except where stated); horizons in ticks; f = cost as a fraction of simulating the question once per member

inputs_paired_with_no_input.note: (N, s_b) under a 200-nat program minus the same branch without input (same noise keys); mean shift, its se over states, and the rms change in units of the no-input branches' sd at that horizon
